name: fault_screen
about: Shows a processor fault on the display instead of a silent hang: the kind of fault, PC, LR, CFSR and the faulting address. HOLD + ROLL on the main screen makes a fault on purpose, to see it work. A debugging aid for mod authors, not for everyday use.

bindings.action: Make a fault on purpose to show the fault screen

hooks.about: HardFault vector word in ITCM; the firmware handler at 0x8003C920 is a lone bx lr
MemManage vector word in ITCM; the firmware handler at 0x800406A8 is a lone bx lr
BusFault vector word in ITCM; the firmware handler at 0x80036118 is a lone bx lr
UsageFault vector word in ITCM; the firmware handler at 0x800437D0 is a lone bx lr
DOOM OS trampoline, ahead of its own handler

task.asked: See what went wrong when a mod crashes the unit, instead of a frozen screen.
task.feasible: Yes. The four fault vectors are plain words in ITCM, the same on every base declared here, and the display can be driven by polling its SPI port without the firmware.
unit_checks: The unit starts and works as on the base firmware.

On the main screen hold HOLD and press ROLL: the screen shows 404LAB FAULT SCREEN with USAGE FAULT or HARD FAULT and a PC inside 0x83FD0000-0x83FD1000. Photograph it, then power off and on: the unit starts normally.
Press HOLD and ROLL separately: each does what it always did.
Use the unit normally for a while, save and reload a project: everything behaves as on the base firmware.
